work_completed: Seven files in `tests/acceptance/W2-92/`, 30 test cases. Each project is a temporary git repository built from scratch: a register with DEC-301 and DEC-302, records CAP-77, REQ-0092, the ticket DAEO-hb92, the lesson LES-0092 (constrains the ticket), W2-592, SPEC-0092 "Cormorant Nesting Protocol", plain pages and three small Python files. Its lexical index, record graph and code index are built in the temp folder with the real `codebase-memory-mcp`. A stand-in for the tool on `PATH` records every request it is sent. It works in both forms the wrapper uses: one-shot `cli` calls and the MCP server session over stdin and stdout. It can also fail on purpose, or the tool can be left off `PATH`. "Today's bundle" has two forms: (1) the base's answers, recorded and written into the test, compared item for item; (2) a live check against the lexical route's fused order. The KPI-to-test map and the red reasons are in the README.

discoveries:
- On the base, the lexical route only matches a chunk holding every word of the question. Any question holding an id (even "lantern note DEC-301" against a page that cites DEC-301) gets an empty bundle today.
- A project whose record graph was never loaded refuses every question, plain ones included, with STORE_MISSING, because W2-87's authority order reads the record graph.
- Today's per-route state is `facets.<route> = {available, reason}`. The stopping reason is already FACET_UNAVAILABLE in every planted bundle, because the semantic route has no vectors.
- `gov.codeintel.callers` talks to the tool as one MCP server session over stdin and stdout, and sends two whole-graph `query_graph` queries (`MATCH (n) …` and `MATCH (a)-[r]->(b) …`, `max_rows` 50000). So a code route built on the existing wrapper or on `gov closure` fails c2.
risks:
- The answers recorded from the base break if a later ticket changes these bundles (W2-13 holds the fusion, W2-55 what is left out); see P-6.
- Earlier retrieval suites (W1-21, W2-87, W1-19, W1-42) may ask questions holding ids or symbol-shaped words, whose bundles would change. I did not check their questions; the lead's re-run will show it.
- The route-state check accepts any `facets` entry or per-route stopping-reason entry that names the route. An unusual form could slip past it or be refused by it (P-2).
- The whole suite needs `gitleaks` and `codebase-memory-mcp`, and cannot run inside the sandbox (the daemon folder there is read-only). The lead runs it outside.
lessons:
- A stand-in for `codebase-memory-mcp` must pass stdin and stdout through line by line. One that waits for the tool to exit deadlocks the wrapper's MCP session; my first version hung.
- The tool's own `trace_path` answers callers on the planted index in about 8 s.
- The lexical route needs every word of the question, so planted texts must share no word with the questions that name them for the red to be real.
proposed_decisions:
- P-1: a missing record store with a question that names no record. Recommend (a): any question answers, with the record route and W2-87's order named unavailable; otherwise (b): keep today's STORE_MISSING for those questions. f3 tests only a question naming a record and a symbol. Confidence medium-low.
- P-2: the form of a route's stopping reason. Recommend today's form, `facets.code` and `facets.closure` (or `facets.records`) = `{available: false, reason}`, with FACET_UNAVAILABLE. The tests also accept a per-route list or mapping. Confidence medium.
- P-3: facet keys added to today's bundle are allowed and best left out. The tests compare today's two facets only; they compare the page a continuation gives, not the token's bytes. Confidence medium.
- P-4: at the default radius 0 the named record joins; its near records join when `radius=1` is given. Confidence medium-high.
- P-5: a ticket id found in a question acts as an `--id`, not a `--ticket`, so no DEC-424 records ahead. Not tested. Confidence low-medium.
- P-6: the recorded answers are revised by a test designer under any later ticket that changes these bundles. Confidence high.
